safety.customHint: Custom Regex matches only the expressions you saved. It can cover email, phone, account/card, IP/URL, and common secrets.

safety.skipToolDeclarationsDetail: Function declarations come from the client and seldom contain personal data, but fields such as MCP server URLs or allowed domains can hold internal addresses or account names. They are inspected by default; when skipped, those values are not replaced.
safety.skipAdditionalToolsHint: additional_tools are function declarations Codex attaches to the conversation input, such as MCP tool names, descriptions, and parameter schemas. The client generates them; they aren't part of what you wrote. Sample emails and links in them are easily flagged by mistake, and replacing them alters the function definitions the model uses to call those tools, so they are skipped by default.

records.modelDurationHint: Model time sums individual model calls, including retries. Active calls update live; gaps between calls are excluded.
records.toolDurationHint: Tool time is estimated from gaps between model calls in the same user turn. It includes client scheduling, network and possible waiting time, excludes gaps between user turns and retry backoff, and is not exact tool execution time.
records.averageTTFTHint: TTFT averages the time from sending the upstream request to receiving the first non-empty text, reasoning or tool call content, using streaming calls with recorded first-token timing.
records.outputSpeedHint: TPS divides total output tokens by total generation time for eligible calls. Generation time is call duration minus TTFT; under 0.5 s (such as output returned in one burst) it counts as 0.5 s. Calls without complete usage or first-token timing are excluded.

records.enableCaptureBody: After you enable body capture, request and response text is stored encrypted in the local database. The key also stays on this machine. If this machine is compromised, that is close to storing plaintext. Enable it?

records.settingsHint: Turn request and response capture on or off with the switch at the top of the page. Only new requests are captured after you enable it. failure.repairHint: Repair is independent of ABC / AABBCC and ordinary retry rules. Each target can be repaired and resent immediately once, within the total attempt limit. Errors after repair follow the error rules.
failure.thinkingSignatureRecoveryHint: For Claude Anthropic requests with thinking signature errors, convert historical thinking to text, remove encrypted thinking, and disable thinking before resending. Repair once per target, independently of retry order, quota, backoff and HTTP error rules. Counts toward the total attempt limit.
failure.openaiReasoningRecovery: Retry after Codex / OpenAI reasoning repair
failure.openaiReasoningRecoveryHint: On explicit Responses reasoning ciphertext or item errors, remove invalid ciphertext or repair the identified item while preserving readable summaries, tool calls and conversation bindings. Repair once per target, independently of ordinary retry rules, within the total attempt limit. Invalid compaction ciphertext is returned as an error.
failure.openaiFunctionOutputRecoveryHint: Off by default. When a Responses request is rejected because function or custom-tool output ciphertext cannot be decrypted, drop those encrypted parts, keep plaintext results, and resend to the same target. Shares one repair per target with reasoning repair and can clear both in the same attempt. Tool call_id pairs stay intact. Independent of ordinary retry rules; counts toward the total attempt limit.
failure.title: Failure handling
failure.serviceHint: Set API provider priority in the API provider list. Error handling inherits defaults unless overridden here.
failure.maxRetriesHint: Excludes the first request and repair requests. 0 disables ordinary retries; maximum 5.
failure.backoffHint: Repeated failures increase the delay, up to 60,000 ms. Longer upstream waits use a backup when switching is allowed.
failure.timeoutHint: 0 means unlimited. This only limits waiting for response headers, not a long reply already streaming.
failure.retryRulesHint: When enabled, continue with the configured retry strategy. Otherwise, return the error.
failure.otherErrors: Enabled request repairs run independently first. If repair is unavailable or fails, error rules apply. Unlisted HTTP errors are returned directly. Replies that have started are never retried, repaired or switched.
failure.invalid: Check retry counts, delays, and error rules. The maximum delay must not be shorter than the first delay.
failure.serviceSummary: Permitted errors get up to {{count}} extra attempts, initially waiting about {{delay}} ms.
failure.enableFailover: Allow switching to a backup target
failure.maxAttemptsHint: Includes the first request, ordinary retries, repair requests, and backups: 1–20 total.
failure.inheritHint: Inherit the default policy unless overridden.
failure.targetRetries: {{name}}: up to {{count}} retries for permitted errors.
failure.retryFirstSummary: Retry the current target, then try backups in order; at most {{count}} total attempts.
failure.failoverFirstSummary: Try unvisited backups first, then revisit targets with retries remaining; at most {{count}} total attempts.
failure.noFailoverSummary: Use only the selected target, without switching; at most {{count}} total attempts.
failure.rulesPrecedence: Error rules control ordinary retries and switching; separate switches control request repair. An attempt limit does not force retries.
failure.globalSwitch: Allow switching API providers after failure
failure.globalOffHint: When automatic switching is off, a failed request does not try another API provider.
failure.loadFailed: Could not load the default policy.

stops.retry_after_limit: Upstream wait exceeds the configured limit
stops.body_not_replayable: Request body cannot be replayed safely

failure.allServicesHint: Configure once for all API providers. Individual API provider settings override these defaults.

failure.inheritOrder: Order and attempt limit inherit Routing → Default policy unless a referenced call path provides its own settings.
failure.defaultsUnavailable: Global settings have not loaded. Reopen the editor after reconnecting to change inherited settings.
failure.onceHint: ABC skips ordinary retries, so retry counts and backoff do not apply. Request repair works independently; error rules still control switching.
failure.failoverOnlySummary: Switch to the next provider after ordinary failures without revisiting. Request repair runs independently; at most {{count}} total attempts, including repairs.
